title: What we truly need in generative AI is better storytelling and interaction
author: Prudent-Goose-6944
selftext:
The rise of Sora and its AI video generation peers has everyone buzzing about their dazzling visuals. But as an AI entrepreneur who's been in this game for nearly a decade, I'm here to tell you: whether it's video or 3D content, the real magic happens when AI helps us tell better stories and create deeper connections.

**This isn't just about people interacting with technology - it's about using AI to spark meaningful human conversations and intellectual collisions. At the end of the day, technology should always serve humanity, not the other way around.**

Over the past year, I've been experimenting with approaches beyond video generation, trying to bring AI into storytelling in ways that feel authentic and human. Because let's be real - no algorithm can replicate our imagination or the emotions we bring to a story.

*If this resonates with you, let's join forces and explore how we can use AI to make storytelling more engaging and accessible for everyone!*

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Define better storytelling.

Do you need every game to be a Shakespeare?

If we need more interconnecting storylines, you can do that but not in a single prompt. You'd need more memory/context.

One way to do this is by building a modular system. One is the overall story. Then one module is to analyze the personality of your characters.

Then use that as input for writing dialogue between these characters. Etc.

The quality of writing increases for every generation, so we will get there. Writing is more difficult to rate than visuals.

replies.author: Prudent-Goose-6944
replies.body: I strongly agree. The progression of the story and feedback between different characters require different models to collaborate.

comments.author: PikachuDash
comments.body:
My AI game is about AI-powered interactive visual novels, so AI storytelling is literally everything it's about. I've thought about prompts and systems for getting the AI to become a superb storyteller for the last 2 years. I have a decent amount of players now, too, and I believe I was successful in my efforts.

Can you elaborate more on what have you experimented with beyond video generation?

replies.author: Prudent-Goose-6944
replies.body: I am trying to return the ability to narrate to users. Specifically, we seem to be making some similar attempts, but the difference is that I hope to turn users' ideas into interactive 3D content using methods similar to previous 3D animation and game production. Users are generating content similar to videos during the 3D interaction process, and video content can serve as an entry point for 3D interaction, enabling real-time switching and interaction across media.

replies.author: PikachuDash
replies.body: I see, that is quite different to what I'm doing. I've seen some content shared about playable 3D worlds created by AI prompts, which sounds similar to what you're experimenting with.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Why does every AI generated game need to have AI as the topic?

comments.author: MrFaabry14
comments.body:
Totally agree. I think part of the issue is how much attention we give to *AI* itself instead of the result.  
I released my first visual novel recently, a gothic, psychological story where narrative and atmosphere are everything. I used AI only as a support tool for the art, but never made it the focus. The story, writing, and design took almost two years, and that’s what players actually connect with.

It’s still early to call it a success, but so far the reception has been very positive, and most people who actually played it don’t even bring up the AI topic, they just talk about the experience. I think that’s the key: be transparent, but let the work speak for itself and ignore the moral crusades that miss the point entirely.
